transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes (record shows 42)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (Zenith Head of Infra), Sofia Reyes (Zenith CISO), Daniel Park (Zenith ML)

Summary: quick weekly checkpoint on the POC (week 3) focused on security/compliance gating items: SSO/SAML testing, audit logs and retention, SOC2 evidence, and a short review of performance numbers from last week's benchmark. Decided action items and timeline for a SSO test and an audit-log config sample.

Topics: Security gating, SSO/SAML metadata, audit log retention and schema, SOC2 artifacts request, Dedicated vs Hosted for pilot, sample benchmark plan, next milestone for go/no-go.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Priya who will lead the security and bench bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark: Doing fine, thanks. Busy week but we got the infra notes in.
[00:11] Sofia: Hi all, brief from my side, I want to make sure we close the SOC2 and log retention questions this week.
[00:17] Priya: Great, we'll start with SOC2 doc ask then move into SSO and logs and then the bench follow-up.
[00:22] Alex: Quick housekeeping — recorded, notes in the doc titled "Zenith POC week 3". No pb.
[00:26] Daniel: Noted. I pulled updated latencies from the last run, will share screen in a sec.
[00:31] Priya: Cool. Sofia, can you confirm the two primary concerns you sent in email — 1) IdP SAML integration and role mapping, 2) audit log retention & exportability?
[00:40] Sofia: Yes exactly. Also KMS integration for our HSM-backed keys, and proof of SOC2 scope for the infra that handles PHI-ish data.
[00:48] Alex: Understood. On SOC2 we can share our latest attestation and the pen-test summary. I'll attach both, they were last updated in Q2.
[00:55] Mark: Are these the same docs you provide to customers or is there an NDA gated package?
[01:00] Alex: Public SOC2 is fine, we also have a more detailed package that we provide under an NDA — but for initial gating the public SOC2 + controls matrix should suffice.
[01:08] Priya: For KMS: we support cloud KMS integrations and HSM via customer-managed keys in the privet package — sorry private — there's a couple typos in our notes but the feature is available. We call out KMS/HSM key wrapping for model artifacts and logs.
[01:20] Sofia: When you say "privet" do you mean Private? Is that the VPC/on-prem deployment?
[01:24] Priya: Yes, private deployment — VPC or on-prem. Sorry for the slip.
[01:27] Daniel: Quick question on audit logs — does Redwood's hosted instance stream logs to our SIEM or do we pull them? What's the retention policy?
[01:34] Priya: Good q. For hosted, we can stream syslog/JSON to your SIEM via secure egress or push to an S3 bucket with server-side encryption. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days in UI, but we can configure export and long-term storage.
[01:46] Mark: Can we set different retention for different log classes — like admin audit vs inference request logs?
[01:50] Priya: Yes, we support per-logtype retention rules, and you can export raw request logs with redaction. Note: by default request bodies may be redacted unless you opt-in for full payload retention for debugging.
[02:02] Sofia: Payload retention opt-in is a blocker. For PHI we cannot retain raw payloads beyond the minimal necessary. We need clear default redaction and documented procedures.
[02:11] Alex: Totally— we'll mark that as an action item. Priya, can you provide the retention template showing defaults and how to opt-in?
[02:16] Priya: Yep, I'll send an example config and the CLI/API snippet that toggles full payload retention and the redaction rules.
[02:22] Daniel: On the bench numbers: last week's run of the 7B model on your Dedicated pool — median p95 latency was 186ms token, throughput was roughly 220 tokens/sec for our typical 32-token prompts. That was with default quant and batching.
[02:36] Priya: Thanks — those numbers align with our internal profile for that model. If you want to lower cost we recommend the quantization profile we discussed and enabling prefix caching for repeated contexts.
[02:45] Mark: Any regression risk from quant? Our outputs are sensitive so we need a small QA set checked after quant change.
[02:50] Priya: Agreed. We can recommend a safe quant profile and run a compare eval on your prompt set — we'll produce diff metrics and sample outputs.
[03:00] Alex: Also to call out routing: if Dedicated capacity is provisioned we'll lock in throughput; if you want failover we can route to a hosted variant with compatible model and lower SLA but better availability.
[03:10] Sofia: For compliance, we prefer Dedicated or Private. Hosted fallback okay for non-PHI traffic but must be opt-in and documented.
[03:18] Priya: Noted. We'll mark Hosted fallback as opt-in per-route.
[03:22] Mark: On SSO — we attempted a SAML exchange earlier but metadata didn't line up, kept failing on NameID format. We think it's our IdP mapping.
[03:31] Alex: Let's do a live SSO test next week. Sofia, can you share the IdP metadata and admin contact?
[03:36] Sofia: Yes I'll share it. Also want to test role mapping and SCIM provisioning if possible.
[03:41] Priya: We support SCIM for user provisioning; role mapping can be handled through our attribute mapping UI or via SAML assertions. We'll bring a short runbook for the SAML attributes.
[03:50] Daniel: Any limitations on session length or token refresh? For inference sessions we'd prefer longer TTLs for cluster efficiency.
[03:56] Priya: Session TTLs are configurable; for security we default shorter, but we can extend for service accounts used by your infra, and recommend rotating keys via KMS.
[04:06] Alex: Going to open the SOC2 packet now in the doc share — I'll put the link in Slack after the call.
[04:10] Mark: Thanks.
[04:12] Sofia: On the legal/comms side: we need an audit-log schema so legal can sign off on e-discovery requests. Does the log include user identifiers, request timestamps, model version, and truncated prompt hashes?
[04:24] Priya: Yes, audit logs include userid, timestamp, model_id, model_version, action (generate/score), and we append a SHA256 truncated hash of the prompt for traceability without full content. Full prompt can be included only if opt-in.
[04:36] Mark: That hash approach will work for us, need to see the exact fields.
[04:40] Daniel: One more note — when you do the benchmark, can we pin model version and disable automatic upgrade? We saw an auto-swap on Friday in our test which broke deterministic outputs.
[04:51] Priya: Yes, you can pin model versions per-route and we also offer canary rollouts — we'll show the rollout UI. Auto-upgrades are not forced for Dedicated.
[05:00] Alex: Alright quick recap before action items. We will share SOC2 and pen-test, Priya will send audit log config + retention template and SAML runbook, schedule SSO test next week, Daniel will run benchmark with pinned model and share results, and Sofia will provide IdP metadata and confirm constraints for PHI. Anything else?
[05:18] Sofia: Please include sample retention SLA language we can paste into our internal docs.
[05:23] Priya: Will do.
[05:24] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the items and set the SSO test.
[05:28] Sofia: Thanks, bye.

Action items (in transcript):
- Alex: Share SOC2 attestation + pen-test (link in Slack)
- Priya: Audit log config + retention template; SAML runbook; SCIM provisioning notes
- Daniel: Run pinned-model benchmark and provide metrics + prompt set
- Sofia: Send IdP metadata and confirm PHI constraints

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional word swaps (KMS noted as K-M-S; "private" transcribed as "privet"), some timestamps approximate.
